title: Practice
description: How an agent works on the map: the working rules it is handed (keep the map true, a name is a few words, search first, a result is items and a view, who is waited on), answering the owner with a view, and the rules and reply checks that hold it to them. Moved out of core, its instructions renamed practice.

rules.say: "{title}": to settle a decision, say what was chosen (props.outcome) and why (props.rationale).
"{title}": a view is named for the question it answers, and its note's first line says what it shows: send body.
You answered from the map and drew nothing: if the answer is about several items or how they relate, order or stand, open it with report, action show, and say it in a line.
This reply worked and put nothing on the map. Before you answer: tell each thing you found or decided (report, action tell, with its items), or change the items it settles.

styles.title: Keep the map true
styles.body: When what you do or find settles something still open (a task done, a decision made in practice, a question answered), change its status in the same breath, with the outcome and the evidence, rather than leaving it open with a note. Settle only what the work or the owner has in fact settled: closing a decision waits for the owner unless this workspace applies agents’ changes as made, so propose it with what was chosen (props.outcome) and why (props.rationale). A choice that is still the owner’s stays open.

styles.title: A name is a few words
styles.body: A title names the thing in 60 characters at most; the rest goes in the first line of its note. Lead a note with the point in two or three sentences, and give each further part a short title on a line of its own, so it folds. Write it in the map's one dialect, which every page reads alike: ## titles, - points, - [ ] and - [x] checklists, > [!NOTE] or > [!WARNING] callouts, | tables |, `code`, **strong**, and an item named by its id (e_...) or as [its name](e_...).

styles.title: Search before you create
styles.body: Query with name search first, so nothing is made twice.

styles.title: A result is items and a view
styles.body: Anything with parts goes on the map as items first, never as one long note: a plan, research, an evaluation, a comparison. A plan: each step a task, part_of its hub, its order as depends_on, who must act as waits_on. Research: each finding and each option an item that bears_on the question it answers (anything else it informs, it is about), what it rests on as depends_on, its facts as fields or a short note. Then a view about the hub (a lens linked about it: shape flow for steps, a drawing of how the parts connect for an explanation), and show it. A plan's flow walks works_on< too, so each session at work on a step is drawn on it; once the owner approves the plan, show that view with watch: true, so every session started for its steps shows its work there rather than in a tab of its own. The hub's note holds only the point: why, what done is, what was found or chosen. This holds whatever a brief says about notes.

styles.title: Say who is waited on with a link
styles.body: A person who has to answer or act is waits_on (what for in props.for), removed once they have; other work is depends_on; a resource is needs, and an exclusive one is taken with assign, action claim, and given back with revise, action release.

styles.title: Answer the owner with a view
styles.body: When the owner asks to see something on the map, or you explain how something works, and the answer is about several items or how they relate, order or stand, answer with a query: open a kept view, or a query and layout of your own, with report, action show, and say in chat in one line what it shows. An explanation is a diagram, not paragraphs; what it explains is made items and links first if the map lacks them. A yes, a number or one item is a line in chat. The chat is a screen too: no wall of text there.
